source_review.notes: Checked all eleven structured primary references at Apache Beam, Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, Reactive Streams, PVLDB, PostgreSQL, Debezium, and CloudEvents on 2026-09-03; every URL returned HTTP 200 and the cited subject was present. Claims about bounded and unbounded collections, durable event logs, bounded/unbounded tables, nonblocking backpressure, event-time processing, logical decoding, change-data capture, and event-envelope identity match the primary texts and remain mechanism-scoped.

evidence: Checked source, epoch, position, occurrence, cut, prefix, delta, fold, materialization, backlog, capacity, lag, and retention notation for consistent domains and units.
Checked that a finite cut is a boundary over source coordinates rather than a claim that an unbounded source has ended.
Checked fold notation preserves event order and keeps the initial state explicit.
Checked backlog recurrence clamps at zero and distinguishes admitted work from serviced work.
Draft chapter validation accepted exact front matter/headings, local links, GitHub mathematics, ten examples, five exercises/answers, and eleven references.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation keeps source existence, finite observation, durable log, changelog semantics, materialized state, processing progress, backlog, and replay capability distinct.

evidence: Executed the annotated model and reproduced six records, the cut-3 materialization A=3/B=4, and the cut-6 materialization A=6/B=3/C=2.
Recomputed prefix totals as 7 at cut 3 and 11 at cut 6.
Recomputed backlog trajectory 0,0,1,0,2 for arrivals 3,5,2,6 at capacity 4, with maximum backlog 2.
Recomputed 16 records accepted, 14 serviced, and 2 pending from the same finite trace.
Independently recomputed Exercise 3 as backlog 0,4,0,1,0 and Exercise 4 as 43.2 million queued records, 3,000 records/s net recovery, and four hours ideal catch-up.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All printed cuts, states, totals, backlog values, conservation values, and Boolean scope claims reproduce under the repository snippet verifier.

evidence: Verified that materialization at cut c is the ordered fold of exactly the source prefix through c over an explicit base state.
Verified backlog conservation as prior backlog plus admitted work minus serviced work, subject to service not exceeding available work.
Verified stable operation requires sustainable service above long-run admitted load with enough margin for variance, failures, checkpointing, and recovery rather than merely equal averages.
Verified replay horizon is limited by the shortest required retained artifact, not solely by broker retention.
Verified an immutable append-only history does not itself make event semantics, authorization, or resulting materialization correct.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Equations are explicit operational models under stated ordering, identity, retention, and resource assumptions, not universal proofs of a deployed streaming system.

evidence: Reviewed empty streams, finite files, mutable tables without snapshots, bounded topic cuts, continuously watched object prefixes, and snapshot-plus-tail sources.
Reviewed missing, duplicate, reordered, corrected, deleted, compacted, truncated, malformed, poison, and semantically incompatible events.
Reviewed partition-local positions without a global order, epoch changes, producer retries, transaction boundaries, hot keys, skew, and rescaling.
Reviewed zero backlog versus hidden upstream lag, average capacity versus bursts, recovery while live traffic continues, retry amplification, sink throttling, and checkpoint stalls.
Reviewed broker bytes retained without schemas, keys, reference generations, state serializers, code/config, authorization, or safe sink repair.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial cases map to explicit source contracts, cut vectors, identity/deduplication semantics, bounded resource policies, durable artifact retention, isolated replay, and conditional publication or repair.

evidence: Checked source identity, epoch, position and occurrence identity remain explicit across capture, storage, processing, materialization, and replay.
Checked every materialization names its exact source cut, base state, transform/schema/reference generations, and publication identity.
Checked progress reporting distinguishes observed, admitted, processed, committed, and consumer-visible frontiers.
Checked overload controls bound admitted work, state, buffers, retries, and sink effects rather than hiding pressure in another queue.
Checked correction and replay append or construct new generations without silently rewriting the historical evidence being audited.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariant set composes finite observation, durable history, semantic interpretation, flow control, retention, and replay into an auditable streaming foundation.

evidence: Reviewed why unbounded describes source membership over time while every actual computation still operates over finite observed prefixes.
Reviewed why an ordered durable log permits multiple cut-relative materializations but does not alone prove business correctness.
Reviewed why backlog recurrence exposes overload and why clearing one finite trace cannot establish long-run stability.
Reviewed why retention must cover the full semantic dependency closure and catch-up duration for replay to be credible.
Reviewed why safe replay requires isolated outputs, deterministic or recorded dependencies, idempotent/fenced effects, reconciliation, and controlled publication.
proof_review.notes: Conclusions are explicitly conditional on correct capture, complete positions, stable identity/order, valid semantics, retained dependencies, sufficient capacity, and verified sink behavior.

evidence: The executable is labeled a finite prefix/backlog demonstration and is not presented as production performance or correctness evidence.
Beam, Kafka, and Flink models are described as concrete framework concepts without treating one product vocabulary as a universal definition.
Reactive Streams backpressure is presented as an interface-level flow-control mechanism, not a guarantee of end-to-end stability or losslessness.
PostgreSQL logical decoding and Debezium CDC are used as capture mechanisms while snapshot, schema, transaction, retention, and sink contracts remain explicit.
The Dataflow paper informs time/completeness framing while later modules retain detailed event-time, window, watermark, and stateful-processing treatment.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Definitions, algebraic reasoning, implementation mechanisms, local examples, operational judgments, and empirical production claims remain visibly separated.

evidence: The local model demonstrates only one six-record delta history and one four-interval backlog trace under fixed service capacity.
HTTP retrieval establishes current primary-source availability/content presence, not installed versions, configured guarantees, or production behavior.
Actual arrival distributions, byte/record/state costs, hot-key skew, checkpoint overhead, sink limits, lag tails, and recovery headroom require measurement.
Actual capture completeness, ordering, duplicate handling, schema compatibility, reference reproducibility, retention, and replay equivalence require deployed audits and drills.
Business correction authority, privacy/deletion obligations, consumer repair semantics, security controls, and acceptable recovery objectives require accountable domain and governance review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No passing snippet, source retrieval, finite arithmetic, log retention setting, or low observed backlog is presented as empirical proof of production correctness, stability, or replayability.
